note: S11.1 (R-lift) base case: cells_rec on a FLAT bridge ($fx.arr = {segments, bindings:{}, off_top:[]}) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to cells_md($fx.arr.segments; T). The bridge carries empty bindings, so no binding has a non-empty .nested.segments → the interior predicate ((.nested.segments // []|length)>0) is false for every cell, the recursion arm never fires, NO path key is attached (omit-when-empty), and cells_rec reduces statement-for-statement to cells_md's per-display _bags fan-out. Reuses the cells_md_split_one_display scene (a v@500 interior gridline homed to d1 splits it into two cells; d2 stays one cell) — the harness emits {eq:bool} comparing the two outputs. This is the in-harness depth-0 proof the recursion attaches no path and never recurses on a flat input.
